summary: Scales a packed 96-bit value in a1 by a table-driven factor derived from the exponent a2. Uses a positive-exponent lookup table rooted at dword_5E9C38 (base - 96 bytes) for a2 > 0 and a negative-exponent table rooted at unk_5E9D98 (base - 96 bytes) after negating a2 when a2 < 0. Consumes the exponent 3 bits (one octal digit) per iteration, advances the table cursor by 84 bytes per digit, selects a 12-byte packed entry by digit, and multiplies the accumulator via sub_597AA0. If a3 is zero, the output *a1 is initialized to zero first. Returns void with the result in a1.

operations.description: Select the default lookup-table base for positive exponents: v3 = (char *)&dword_5E9C38[-24], i.e. dword_5E9C38 minus 96 bytes.
Early-out when a2 is zero: nothing is written to a1 and the function returns.
When a2 < 0, negate a2 and switch the table base to unk_5E9D98 - 96 (reciprocal-power table).
When a3 is zero, initialize the output *a1 to 0 before the decoding loop.
Iterate while a2 != 0, consuming 3 bits per iteration: a2 >>= 3 and digit v5 = v4 & 7 where v4 is the low byte of a2.
Advance the table cursor by one section per octal digit: v3 += 84.
Only non-zero digits are processed; a zero digit (v5 == 0) skips the table lookup and multiply for this step.
Select the 12-byte packed entry for the digit: v6 = &v3[12 * v5].
When the first word of the entry is >= 0x8000 the entry is in an extended form: expand 12 bytes into a local 96-bit value (8-byte v8 plus 4-byte v9) and decrement one middle dword.
Multiply the accumulated packed value in a1 by the selected table entry via sub_597AA0 for this digit.
Void return; the scaled packed result is delivered in a1.
